u2fd: Always enable user keys This change deprecates the "legacy" code path, and enables legacy fallback if users have not swiched explicitly to the new code path. This is a forced migration to the new code path, while still supporting legacy key handles for authentication. For a user who has previously enabled U2F with 'u2f' or 'g2f' mode (but not switched to user keys), this change will cause new registrations to be user-specific, but old keys can still be used to authenticate. No user action is required for this behavior. shill: Connection: Remove Request/ReleaseRouting This patch prepares te removal of Connection from PortalDetector and HttopRequest. Calls to Connection::RequestRouting and ::ReleaseRouting are moved from HttpRequest to Device. Since the latter knows when a full multi probe trial is finished, it can call RequestRouting and ReleaseRouting exactly once, which remove the need for ref counting the number of RequestRouting calls. Since there is no other user of these two methods, they are also removed from Connection. BUG=b:136710574 BUG=b:136710873 TEST=1) "FEATURE=test emerge-eve shill" passed. 2) manual captive portal connection tests with real portal networks. shill: Remove Connection from PortalDetector This patch removes Connection as a member variable in PortalDetector and instead makes Device and ConnectionDiagnostic pass either two lists of DNS addresses for IPv4 and IPv6, or a single list and an IP family to PortalDetector::StartAfterDelay when a portal detection trial is started. This prepares for making PortalDetector aware of layer 3 informations like DNS address list so that a single Trial can retry over different IP families on dual stack networks. Since the most likely place to pass the freshest layer 3 information is PortalDetector::StartAfterDelay(), this patch also consolidates into one function ::StartAfterDelay(), ::StartTrialAfterDelay(), and ::StartTrial(), and adds ::UpdateAttemptTime as well. This allows to avoid carrying the same arguments forward from one function to the next. BUG=b:136710574 BUG=b:136710873 TEST=1) "FEATURE=test emerge-eve shill" passed, 2) manual portal detection checks Change-Id: I62c721c7765d8d8982b9f283a08099d6f37c9df7 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1697987 Tested-by: Matthew Wang <matthewmwang@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org>

chaps: Use crypto::ScopedEVP_MD_CTX OpenSSL 1.1 will use _new()/_free() semantics for all CTX types. 1.0 already does so for EVP_MD_CTX, so we can do the switch now, and, while we are at it, use the recommended _ex() forms for Init and Final. Furthermore, let's used the Scoped* version for better pointer lifetime tracking. Since we are just storing a unique_ptr in the struct, we can now pull it out of the union without bloating the struct size significantly. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:738288 TEST=FEATURES=test emerge-sarien chaps Change-Id: I497fa694a406b744d31af944c128192a5888092c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1757197 Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org>

bluetooth: implement DebugManager for btdispatch DebugManager exposes a D-Bus API to specify the debug verbosity level for dispatcher, newblue, bluez, and kernel. In this patch, only the D-Bus connection and some writing and reading from/to config files (which inits the value of debug verbosity) that has been implemented. The part of printing logs based on these values, is not yet implemented. BUG=chromium:734152 TEST=Do the following. 1) Use the new API dbus-send --system --print-reply --dest=org.chromium.Bluetooth \ /org/chromium/Bluetooth org.chromium.Bluetooth.Debug.SetLevels \ byte:<dispatcher_verbosity> \ byte:<newblue_verbosity> \ byte:<bluez_verbosity> \ byte:<kernel_verbosity> 2) Check the debug conf files on /var/lib/bluetooth/debug.conf contains the actual verbosity level set on step 1. 3) Check the D-Bus property also contains the actual verbosity level. dbus-send --system --dest=org.chromium.Bluetooth --print-reply \ /org/chromium/Bluetooth org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get \ string:org.chromium.Bluetooth.Debug string:<property> Where <property> is one of these below {DispatcherLevel, NewblueLevel, BluezLevel, KernelLevel} Cq-Depend: chromium:1708230,chromium:1728790 Change-Id: I49c679e549d9f3076dcc60e110a25aa7e4387398 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1725690 Tested-by: Archie Pusaka <apusaka@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Archie Pusaka <apusaka@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org>

mount-encrypted: add the new cmdline option "insecure" mount-encrypted doesn't store an insecure system key in NVRAM, which allows us to keep encstateful not wiped over TPM clearing and avoids potential unexpected behavior caused by soft-clearing TPM 2.0. The option should only be enabled for testing purposes and will be used in the autotest env. This CL provdes an alternative and simpler way to solve the soft-clearing TPM 2.0 problem mentioned above, compared with the original solution in CL:1753389. BUG=b:139399088 TEST=tested along with CL:1763468: On a chell, make sure the changes are no-op in any case. On a soraka, create the magic file in /mnt/stateful_partition, then 1. Run crossystem to clear the TPM, reboot, and log in. Then, repeat those 3 steps a few times and make sure each time the encrypted partition is not wiped. Also, check if mount-encrypted.log says it uses an insecure system key. 2. Run tpm_softclear to soft-clear the TPM, then run tpm_manager_client take_ownership to re-own the TPM, then reboot. Make sure the encrypted partition isn't wiped and mount-encrypted.log says it uses an insecure system key. 3. Remove the magic file, run crossystem to clear the TPM, reboot, and make sure the encrypted partition is wiped and mount-encrypted.log says it creates a random key and stores it in NVRAM. Change-Id: I68c762de6115ec33e3ea7ebc35f50f7264578b21 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1763467 Tested-by: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org>

shill: vpn: Stop overridding SetConnection CL:1748120 introduced a regression by triggering a latent infinite loop that was not previously reachable because the previous SetConnection override did not work as "intended". Ever since it was introduced in CL:22461, the VPNService::SetConnection override essentially behaved as if it wasn't there at all. Since Device::DestroyConnection calls Service::SetConnection(nullptr) prior to destroying the Connection instance, and since rebinding a Binder does *not* cause--nor has it ever caused--the client_disconnect_callback to be called, the Binder in VPNService::SetConnection was never bound to a Connection during the destruction of the Connection. This change simply removes the override of SetConnection, as the previous implementation essentially behaved as if that was the case. BUG=chromium:996957 TEST=-All unit tests are passing. -Triggering a VPN disconnect after successfully connecting does not cause VPNDriver::OnConnectionDisconnected to be called (as was the behavior before CL:1748120). With l2tp, this is verified with: `cat /var/log/net.log | grep Underlying` Change-Id: Ief557c9b429dd55bedffc3aefaec4f1b6e6db680 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1769576 Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>
